records.found: Nothing dated in the window turned up: the searches returned the 2020 Unity Biotechnology knee trial, the Steadman Philippon fisetin trial and the withdrawn trial called ROPE, all already in this entry's notes. They also returned a second Steadman Philippon trial that the entry does not name. I searched the treatment, paper, claim and self-experiment records for its registry number and for 'losartan' and found neither. Its registry entry, opened on the registry's data interface, shows: 'Use of Senolytic and Anti-Fibrotic Agents to Improve the Beneficial Effect of Bone Marrow Stem Cells for Osteoarthritis' (registry number NCT04815902), 100 people with knee osteoarthritis, four groups (fisetin with losartan, fisetin alone, losartan alone, placebo for both), every group also given an injection of concentrated bone marrow; started 2021-05-18, last updated 2024-04-16, status unknown, no results posted. Its main measure is safety, so even with results it would not meet this entry's test as written. A suspended Assiut University trial of quercetin and fisetin with a third drug (20 people) was seen in a search result only.

records.found: Nothing dated in the window turned up, and no report of longer telomeres in a person after a telomerase gene therapy. The searches returned the 2019 Colombian trial and the 2025 report of two patients given cells treated with the gene ZSCAN4, both already in this entry. They also returned a registered telomerase gene therapy trial in people that the entry does not name. I searched the treatment, paper, claim and self-experiment records for its registry number, its drug name, 'dilated cardiomyopathy', 'Shanghai East' and 'Tongji' and found none. Its registry entry, opened on the registry's data interface, shows: 'Myocardial Telomere Recapping Study for Dilated Cardiomyopathy' (registry number NCT05837143), sponsored by Shanghai East Hospital with the company Shanghai Juvensis Therapeutics; a single infusion into the heart's arteries of a harmless virus carrying a modified telomerase gene, switched on in heart muscle; 12 people enrolled; started 2023-03-30; last updated 2024-07-16 with status unknown; no results posted. It does not list telomere length or cancer rate among its measures, so it does not meet the first human test.
records.for_john: An older record the entry missed, not a result in the window. The change I would have made: a dated note, beside the one on the Colombian trial, saying the registry holds a second trial of a telomerase gene therapy in people (registry number NCT05837143, Shanghai East Hospital with Shanghai Juvensis Therapeutics, 12 people with heart failure from an enlarged, weakened heart, one infusion of a virus carrying a modified telomerase gene, started 2023-03-30, status unknown since the update of 2024-07-16, no results, and neither telomere length nor cancer rate among its listed measures). The estimate's dated note says the registry holds one such trial; this makes two, and the entry's 'far' reasoning may want to weigh that twelve people appear to have been dosed. The first human rung does not move: no peer-reviewed report, no telomere measurement. It is not mine to make because a reading does not edit notes or estimates on an older record. Source opened: the registry entry. Seen in a search result only and not opened, and I doubt it: an aggregator brief dated 2026-03-28 (the-teknologist.pages.dev, 'biotech longevity brief 2026-03-28') saying the company Rejuvenate Bio dosed a first person with a telomerase gene therapy; no company release or registry entry for it was returned.
